sentence.text: We know of no lab that binds every published number to bytes at a commit (where sworn's neighbours bind numerals, artifacts and structured assertions, as the 2026-09-05 survey names them), re-derives every verdict from those bytes into a chained log (where Certificate Transparency and Rekor chain certificates and signed metadata, not verdicts), gives every receipt a face a stranger reads without json (where random art gives a host key one and an identicon gives an address one), fingerprints a model's behavior on hashed canaries against a measured null floor (where Dutta et al. measure flips and KL divergence under compression, and Thinking Machines measure the same-weights spread of served completions), and pays a standing bounty against its own verifier (where Immunefi pays against deployed code and the Preregistration Challenge paid for preregistering) — at once. The seal on a public chain is not in this sentence: OpenTimestamps does that for any document, and has since 2016.

S01.title: Hash Visualization: a New Technique to Improve Real-World Security

C3.object: public-key fingerprints and root keys, compared by eye
C3.quote: The visual fingerprints generated by Random Art are clearly easier to compare than the hexadecimal representation.
render SSH host keys in a visual form that is amenable to easy recall and rejection of changed host keys

S04.title: How To Time-Stamp a Digital Document

C4b.object: any digital document, through a time-stamping service (from the pages read; the linking scheme in later sections was not read)
C4b.quote: We propose computationally practical procedures for digital time-stamping of such documents so that it is infeasible for a user either to back-date or to forward-date his document

C4b.object: any data, anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain, independently verifiable — a preregistration is data
C4b.quote: A timestamp proves that some data existed prior to some point in time. OpenTimestamps defines a set of operations for creating provable timestamps and later independently verifying them.

S06.title: Proof of Existence
S06.pages_read: the archived page carries only its title; the application is a script shell

C2.object: certificates in an append-only Merkle log with a signed tree head, checked by monitors — the same mechanism for a different object
C2.quote: The append-only property of each log is technically achieved using Merkle Trees, which can be used to show that any particular version of the log is a superset of any previous version.

C2.object: signed supply-chain metadata in an append-only ledger audited for consistency
C2.quote: Rekor aims to provide an immutable, tamper-resistant ledger of metadata generated within a software project's supply chain.

S11.title: How Is ChatGPT's Behavior Changing over Time?

S12.title: Accuracy is Not All You Need

C4a.object: compressed versus baseline models by KL divergence over token distributions and per-item flips on benchmark sets; no hashed canary set, no in-situ same-weights floor, no verdict with an interval — the nearest neighbour of the checksum's measurement
C4a.quote: We propose two such metrics, KL-Divergence and % flips, and show that they are well correlated.

S13.title: Instructional Fingerprinting of Large Language Models

C4a.object: an ownership fingerprint implanted by fine-tuning and verified by its trigger

S14.title: REEF: Representation Encoding Fingerprints for Large Language Models

C4a.object: centered-kernel-alignment similarity of two models' representations on the same samples, to decide derivation — a neighbour of the belief-geometry agreement
C4a.quote: REEF computes and compares the centered kernel alignment similarity between the representations of a suspect model and a victim model on the same samples.

S15.title: Representational similarity analysis - connecting the branches of systems neuroscience

C4a.object: representational dissimilarity matrices compared across systems by correlation of their upper triangles, with a noise floor — the rdm_r half of the fingerprint, for brains
C4a.quote: RDMs can be quantitatively compared using correlation distance (1-correlation) or rank-correlation distance.
